title: Quarrel with Max Kaminsky over the amplifier and quitting
summary: Zutty complained to Max Kaminsky, who promised to turn the speaker down but made it louder; Zutty called him a phony and left. A Notre Dame bandleader sympathized, and Marge had begged him to quit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And Maxie Kaminsky, I told him about it. I said, man, you sitting and sitting right here and I'm right on the end, see, playing the drums. And Marshall Brown is over there.
The speaker is over here?

Yes. Well he's got this loud speaker over here by me, see. And one night I told Maxie about this. And one night I told, I saw Maxie telling Marshal to turn it up a little. And Marshal came up Brown, you know....
And made it louder.
A little louder and that's when I called Maxie a phony. He said, well I'm going to let you go tonight.
But I told Zutty ......
Claude Hopkins was playing piano.
Who?

Claude Hopkins was playing piano that night because Bobby Pratt had laid off or something. And I told Maxie, I said man, you're a phony! He said, what you say? I said, I say you're a phony! Because he told me that he was going to have Marshall to soften it down a little.
But then Mattie he didn't want Zutty to come out and he told Max you know.
But you did come out?
Oh yes.
And I was glad because I'd been after him to quit anyway.
Yes, but you came out sort of mad?
Yes, yes.
So then that probably played on you.
Sure, sure.
But what they were doing with this electronic stuff was.....

Marshall, you know a band leader from Notre Dame came in one night, that's when Notre Dame played somebody here in New York. And he told me, he said, Zutty, how can you stand that kind of stuff that's going on? He said, because I'm listening to you. See, because he knows the difference. This guy asked me, he was from Notre Dame wasn't he?
Yes. They had played football here that day.
O'Brian.

But I begged Zutty to quit because I could see it coming on. And he knows, I told him two or three times. Say you're bringing your blood pressure up. I'm saying it facetiously but I'd tell him. I'd say listen Zutty we'll live on your pension and our social security. We can get social security. I was getting my social security. And we'll just live on that. Who needs it? And we'd go on and he'd say, well you know Mattas wanting me in there so badly.
Well I tell you, that would give me blood pressure.
